metadata.name: Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA)
metadata.summary: 8-item bedside clinical scale (0–40) quantifying cerebellar ataxia severity across gait, stance, sitting, speech, and limb coordination.
clinical_pearls: Items 5–8 (limb kinetic tests) are tested bilaterally; if left and right differ, enter the mean of both sides.
Total score ranges from 0 (no ataxia) to 40 (most severe ataxia).
Demonstrates high interrater reliability (ICC 0.98), test-retest reliability (ICC 0.90), and internal consistency (Cronbach alpha 0.94) in cerebellar ataxia (Schmitz-Hübsch et al., 2006).

Pitfall — Non-cerebellar confounders & oculomotor omission: Pyramidal weakness, spasticity, sensory loss, or orthopedic limitations can inflate gait/limb scores, and SARA does not score oculomotor signs (e.g., nystagmus or saccadic dysmetria).

items.label: Gait
items.subtitle: Walk a safe distance parallel to a wall including a half-turn and tandem walk

options.label: Normal, no difficulties in walking, turning, or walking tandem
Slight difficulties, only visible when walking 10 consecutive steps in tandem
Clearly abnormal; tandem walking > 10 steps not possible
Considerable staggering, difficulties in half-turn, but without support
Marked staggering, intermittent support of the wall required
Severe staggering, permanent support of one stick or light support by one arm required
Walking > 10 m only with strong support (two special sticks or stroller or accompanying person)
Walking < 10 m only with strong support
Unable to walk, even supported

items.label: Stance
items.subtitle: Stand in natural position, feet together, and tandem for 10 seconds

options.label: Normal, able to stand in tandem for > 10 s
Able to stand with feet together without sway, but not in tandem for > 10 s
Able to stand with feet together for > 10 s, but only with sway
Able to stand for > 10 s without support in natural position, but not with feet together
Able to stand for > 10 s in natural position only with intermittent support
Able to stand for > 10 s in natural position only with constant support of one arm
Unable to stand for > 10 s even with constant support of one arm

items.label: Sitting
items.subtitle: Sit on examination bed without support of feet, eyes open, arms outstretched

options.label: Normal, no difficulties sitting > 10 s
Slight difficulties, intermittent sway
Constant sway, but able to sit > 10 s without support
Able to sit for > 10 s only with intermittent support
Unable to sit for > 10 s without continuous support
Normal
Suggestion of speech disturbance
Impaired speech, but easy to understand
Occasional words difficult to understand
Many words difficult to understand
Only single words understandable
Speech unintelligible / anarthria

items.label: Finger Chase
items.subtitle: Mean of right and left sides (5 consecutive sudden movements)

options.label: No dysmetria
Dysmetria, under/overshooting target < 5 cm
Dysmetria, under/overshooting target < 15 cm
Dysmetria, under/overshooting target > 15 cm
Unable to perform 5 pointing movements

items.label: Nose-Finger Test
items.subtitle: Mean of right and left sides (kinetic tremor amplitude)

options.label: No tremor
Tremor with an amplitude < 2 cm
Tremor with an amplitude < 5 cm
Tremor with an amplitude > 5 cm
Unable to perform 5 pointing movements

items.label: Fast Alternating Hand Movements
items.subtitle: Mean of right and left sides (10 cycles of pronation/supination on thigh)

options.label: Normal, no irregularities (performs < 10 s)
Slightly irregular (performs < 10 s)
Clearly irregular, single movements difficult to distinguish or relevant interruptions, but performs < 10 s
Very irregular, single movements difficult to distinguish or relevant interruptions, performs > 10 s
Unable to complete 10 cycles

items.label: Heel-Shin Slide
items.subtitle: Mean of right and left sides (3 slides along tibia)

options.label: Normal
Slightly abnormal, contact to shin maintained
Clearly abnormal, goes off shin up to 3 times during 3 cycles
Severely abnormal, goes off shin 4 or more times during 3 cycles
Unable to perform the task

interpretation.label: No Ataxia (0 pts)
interpretation.summary: No clinical signs of cerebellar ataxia on examination.

interpretation.label: Mild Ataxia (1–14 pts)
interpretation.summary: Mild cerebellar dysfunction; typically ambulatory without walking aids.
interpretation.clinical_note: SARA is a continuous severity measure; 1–14 / 15–24 / >=25 are pragmatic clinical strata.

interpretation.label: Moderate Ataxia (15–24 pts)
interpretation.summary: Moderate ataxia; often requires walking aid or assistance for gait and daily tasks.

interpretation.label: Severe Ataxia (25–40 pts)
interpretation.summary: Severe ataxia; typically wheelchair-dependent or unable to stand/sit unsupported.

assessment_guides.title: Bilateral Averaging for Items 5–8
bedside_steps: Examine items 5 (Finger Chase), 6 (Nose-Finger), 7 (Fast Alternating Hand Movements), and 8 (Heel-Shin Slide) on both right and left sides separately.
If scores differ between sides, take the arithmetic mean (if a half-point results in asymmetric ataxia, round to the nearest integer in this 1-point selector).
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Do not score weakness or spasticity as ataxia if the task cannot be performed solely due to pyramidal paresis—document confounding deficits separately.

references.citation: Schmitz-Hübsch T, du Montcel ST, Baliko L, et al. Scale for the assessment and rating of ataxia: development of a new clinical scale. Neurology. 2006;66(11):1717-1720.
